title: Factorial-Gevrey weights have a sharp one-radius absorption boundary at p equals one

gevrey_boundary.weights: a_n(R,p)=R^n/(n!)^p for R>0 and p>0; the spectral multiplier is entire in q for every p>0
gevrey_boundary.shift_moment: a_(n-1)/a_n=n^p/R, so AM-GM bounds the shifted hierarchy by G/2+D_p/(2R), D_p=sum n^p a_n F_n
gevrey_boundary.radius_derivative: Differentiating R-dependent weights supplies (R'/R)D_1 and no higher moment
gevrey_boundary.absorbable_range: For 0<p<=1, n^p<=n permits absorption by one decreasing radius; for p>1, D_p/D_1 is unbounded on a single high tier
gevrey_boundary.global_boundary: Every absorbable p still needs an additive negative radius speed proportional to B, so B>=1 forces finite-time radius loss by K1453
gevrey_boundary.ceiling: The result classifies this diagonal entire one-parameter family only; it does not exclude sign-sensitive spacetime estimates, multiple radii or nonlinear modified energies
